matchstick.title: Single‑stick numeral reduction
matchstick.principle: If two Roman numerals differ by exactly one stick, you can move that stick to change one numeral into the other while keeping both characters valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you notice that a numeral could become another valid numeral by adding or removing a single stick.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from a V and leaving the V as a single diagonal line (invalid numeral).

matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: Never rotate a stick; its orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) must stay the same after moving.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you relocate a stick, keep its original orientation.
matchstick.example: Treating a diagonal stick as a vertical stick when moving it to form an I.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: You must move exactly one existing stick; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of planning a move, verify you are only relocating a stick.
matchstick.example: Adding an extra vertical stick to an I to make II without removing any stick elsewhere.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After the move, each symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral or an allowed operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any stick relocation, check every character for validity.
matchstick.example: Turning a V into a single diagonal line, which is not a Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Compute the Arabic values of both sides of the equation and ensure they are equal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a candidate transformed equation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Accepting 'XV - XV = XVI' without noticing that 15 − 15 ≠ 16.

matchstick.title: Operator swap via stick exchange
matchstick.principle: You may move a stick from one operator to another, changing both operators, as long as the resulting symbols are still valid operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains two operators (e.g., '=' and '-') and a stick can be transferred between them.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=' to '-' and ending up with a single '-' (invalid) on the left side.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: Never remove a stick from X or V, because the remaining single diagonal is not a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before removing a stick from any X or V, verify that the resulting shape is still a valid numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from X, leaving a lone diagonal line.

matchstick.title: Cross‑numeral stick transfer
matchstick.principle: A stick can be moved from one numeral to another, provided both the source and destination remain valid numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to adjust the values of two numerals by transferring a stick.
matchstick.example: Taking a diagonal from a V and adding it to an X, leaving the V as a single diagonal (invalid).

matchstick.title: Within‑numeral stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A stick may be repositioned within the same numeral (e.g., moving a diagonal in V to create X) as long as its orientation stays the same and the resulting numeral is valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single numeral can be changed by moving one of its sticks internally.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal of a V to cross the other diagonal but placing it incorrectly, resulting in an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Equality sign preservation
matchstick.principle: The equation must contain exactly one '=' sign after the move; you cannot turn it into another operator or remove one of its horizontal bars.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider moving a stick that belongs to the '=' sign.
matchstick.example: Moving one of the two horizontal sticks from '=' to '-' and ending up with a single '-' instead of an equality sign.

matchstick.description: Rotating sticks (treating a diagonal as vertical or vice‑versa)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes sticks are interchangeable regardless of orientation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Keep the original orientation of each stick; you may only relocate it without rotating.

matchstick.description: Adding or removing sticks instead of moving exactly one
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model confuses moving with creating or deleting sticks.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure exactly one existing stick is relocated; no sticks are added or removed.

matchstick.description: Creating invalid numerals after a move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on arithmetic change without checking character validity.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After moving a stick, verify each numeral is a recognized Roman numeral.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model stops after finding a plausible‑looking transformation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the Arabic values of both sides and confirm equality.

matchstick.description: Changing operators to disallowed symbols (e.g., turning ‘=’ into ‘≠’)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tries to modify operators without remembering the allowed set.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only use the permitted operators (+, -, =) after any stick move.
